newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russian prosecutor probes mafia links in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Russian prosecutor probes mafia links in Geneva.

text.p: Russia's Prosecutor-General Yuri Skuratov met justice officials in Geneva on Wednesday to cooperate against organised crime in the city, Switzerland's main banking hub and a secretive haven for offshore wealth.
Switzerland is anxious to protect its reputation as a safe haven for the world's very rich and ensure that its banks are not implicated in Russian mafia-related activities.

Swiss news agency ATS said Skuratov was looking into the case of a Russian, Sergei Mikhailov, who was arrested in Geneva in October and is being investigated on charges of criminal links and money-laundering.
A Geneva court has extended the 38-year-old Russian's detention and police is investigating his connections.
Mikhailov's arrest has caused concern among Swiss authorities, who have pledged to take extra measures against the threat of inflows of potentially-dirty money from Russia.
Swiss private bankers say the collapse of communism in Russia has created enormous private wealth which is flowing into Switzerland, the world's number one private banking centre.

Banking sources say Russian deposits at Swiss banks have more than doubed to well over $3 billion in the past years and, with capital flight from Russia running at hundreds of millions of dollars every month, are likely to increase further.

Some Swiss banks have a blanket policy of not accepting any Russian clients while others have established centralised units to deal with Russians. Several banks have a so-called "white gloves" policy to detect money with suspicious origins.
ATS quoted Geneva's Public Prosecutor Jean-Louis Crochet as saying after talks with Skuratov that Russia had offered full support to Switzerland in fighting organised crime.
Skuratov, in Switzerland on a four-day trip, met Swiss Federal Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte in Berne on Tuesday. His visit included talks with regional prosecutors in Zurich.

Del Ponte said last year that she had evidence that Russian gangs were trying to move their crime profits into Switzerland despite anti-money laundering laws that have been tightened since the late 1980s.
